_comment: Everything in the data folder is bundled: each folder directly under 'root' becomes one asset (one archive), found automatically. The 'exclude' list says what is NOT bundled (and what an extraction never overwrites): whole folders, and files that belong to the repo or the server. The 'ignore' list is the same kind of pattern list for junk inside the folders being bundled (editor backups, temp files, OS litter); it is applied exactly like 'exclude', and bundle-assets --ignore PATTERN / ASSETS_IGNORE add to it for one run or for good outside the file. Patterns are relative to 'root', gitignore style: a name without '/' matches that name anywhere (a folder is left out whole), a pattern with '/' matches that path; * and ? work. 'required': assets whose absence fails a bundle or setup run; every other asset is optional (skipped with a warning). 'optional': names to know even when the folder is not on this machine (so setup-data --only can ask for them). 'on_demand': assets that are bundled and uploaded as usual but that setup-data downloads only when asked for by name (--only or ASSETS), because nothing at runtime needs them (data/spam is the 109 MB MapSPAM source; the cassava mask built from it is tracked in git). 'archives': archive names that differ from <name>-data.tar.gz. 'split_over_mb': a file larger than this goes into an archive of its own (<name>-data-<file>.tar.gz) and the smaller files stay together in the asset's main archive, so changing one big file re-uploads that file, not the whole asset. 'human_sizes': also write sizes as text ('1.4 MiB') next to the byte counts in manifest.json (bundle-assets --human-sizes / --no-human-sizes overrides it). 'compress_level' (gzip, 0-9) is used for archives whose files can shrink; archives made only of 'already_compressed' file types are stored without recompressing (gzip makes .rds bigger and slower for no gain). Narrow a run with --only/--exclude, or for good with ASSETS / ASSETS_EXCLUDE.
